summary: Nothing new to add in this final cycle; the draft bytes are the correction landed last cycle (install-path Fact at revision 2, changed_premise 68e8d28ce0d24ceab7d8ada23a81f56c-knowledge-0@1), so no duplicate revision is created. Final record for the independent reviewer: one asserted defect - shouldSnapshot compares the log store's last index with the cached snapshot index as unsigned values, so a node whose store sits below its snapshot index reports that it should snapshot even when applied and commit indices already equal the snapshot. It is witnessed twice over real producers: after a TrailingLogs=0 user snapshot emptied the store (CheckRun 9cba2e79ff6c4019b0f0381690d9aaab: control false, then store_last=0 against snapshot_index=4 with commit/applied still 4 gives true) and after a follower installed a snapshot above its own log store (CheckRun e5116cfe896549deb27799d6d871ed77: snapshot_index=8, store_last=5, should_snapshot=true, with the leader's snapshot taken while the follower was isolated). The consequence is measured as redundant snapshot attempts at the unchanged index (CheckRun a4a0cbfa094b4d1982032d9de0652861, counts 1 to 3 with the applied index fixed) and bounded to wasted snapshot work with no safety effect; the attempt cadence stays unmeasured and both durable Facts were corrected to drop the withdrawn per-interval implication. Three suspicions are refuted with retained operands: a non-voter acknowledgement cannot advance commitIndex (a withheld non-voter changed nothing; a stored-but-uncommitted entry shows the non-voter is ignored), a restart preserves the durable last vote so one node cannot cast two different votes in a term (applicable=true receipt), and the AddVoter configuration lag is a bounded replication transient (2ms old config, new by 102ms), with the user-restore and non-quiescent install routes also measured not to produce the snapshot condition.
